Now hereupon the Apostle glories in them, as men are apt to do in the Heroick Acts of great Conquerours, or the Captain of an Army, in the valiant performances of his Soul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />diers.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:523" />5 <ns0:hi>Which is</ns0:hi> a manifest token of the righteous judgment of God <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">These words seem to follow by way of Argument, to com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fort these <ns0:hi>Thessalonians</ns0:hi> under their sufferings. 1. By what they manifest, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> the righteous judgment of God. They are a plain indication of it, or demonstration, as the word is used by Logicians: And by judgment we must not here understand the judgments or afflictions, God inflicts in this World; so that when God doth not spare, but chasten his own children, it is a token of his righteous Judgment. But ra<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="3 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>•••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>r under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand it of the last Judgment, when we see the righteous suf<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fering such wrongs and injuries from wicked men, and they go unpunished, we may argue thence that there is a judgment to come. We cannot else well vindicate the righteousness, Wis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom, Goodness and Faithfulness of God in his governing the World: As <ns0:hi>Solomon</ns0:hi> so argued, when he saw so much unrigh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teousness in the very sea<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> of Justice, <ns0:hi>I said in my heart, God will judge the righteous, and the wicked, for there is a time for every purpose and work Eccles.</ns0:hi> 3.16, 17. And this judgment is called here <ns0:hi>righteous judgment,</ns0:hi> by way of eminency; As its expressed by one word, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 2.5, 6. (for all Gods judgments are righteous) 1. Because the wicked will then meet with justice without mercy, which is not so in any pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sent judgments. 2. Justice will then be clearly manifested, which now lies obscure, both with respect to the righteous and the unrighteous. And in this sence the words carry an Argu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment of comfort to the Saints, under their present unjust suf<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ferings from their enemies. As to the same purpose the Apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stle speaks to the <ns0:hi>Philippians, Phil.</ns0:hi> 1.28. vid.</ns0:note>, that ye may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">2. The o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther argument of comfort is from the result of their sufferings, the great advantage which will arise out of them. They will be hence accounted worthy of the Kingdom of God, not by way of merit, as the Papists say. The Greek word in the Text in its usual acceptation, will not favour that opinion, it signi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fies no more in the Active voice, then the Latin word <ns0:hi>dignari,</ns0:hi> which we English to deign, or vouchsafe; and yet we may allow the word to signifie more here, not only that this King<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom may be vouchsafed, but that ye may be meet, or worthy to receive it, not that all their sufferings could deserve this Kingdom, for the Apostle saith, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.18. I <ns0:hi>reckon the sufferings of this present time not worthy of the glory, &c.</ns0:hi> There is no pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />portion betwixt them, and so they can<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> merit it, yet God may account those that suffer for this Kingdom worthy of it, according to the grace of the New Covenant in Jesus Christ<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and as it hath a congruity with the nature of God, and his faithfulness in his promises, and so our Translation renders the word: Not that ye may be worthy of the Kingdom of God, but accounted worthy. God of his free grace will account them worthy. The Kingdom of God is propounded <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> men in the new Covenant, upon certain conditions, and those that perform them have a worthiness of <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ight: As, <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 22.14. but not of merit. But God enables men to perform the conditi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons, so that there is nothing on our part properly meritorious, yea, when we have performed them, yet our worthiness is to be attributed to Christ, and Gods grace, and not to our selves, else man would have whereof to glory. The Scriptures call Eternal Life the gift of God, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 6. <ns0:hi>last,</ns0:hi> and attributes sal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vation to grace, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 2.8. We must allow a worthiness only that is consis<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ent with grace: But when we have done all, we must say, <ns0:hi>we are, unprofitable servants, L<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ke</ns0:hi> 17.10. And after all we have done and suffered for the Kingdom of God, must pray as <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> for <ns0:hi>Onesiphorus,</ns0:hi> that we may find mercy of the Lord at that day, 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1.18.</ns0:note>, for which ye also suffer <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">The sence either respects their enemies, that it was upon the account of this Kingdom, that they persecuted them; having nothing else justly against them. Or else their own aim and intention in suffering, it was for the Kingdom of God: And whence we may learn that this King<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom is worth suffering for, and that in some cases cannot be obtained without suffering. And he that then refuseth to suf<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fer will be accounted unworthy of it, as he that doth suffer for it, as these <ns0:hi>Thessalonians</ns0:hi> hath, upon the account of Gods Cove<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nant, and the merits of Christ, not only the grace and mercy, but the justice and faithfulness of God ingaged to bestow it upon him. And also that we may and ought in our sufferings look to the reward, as <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> did <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 11.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 Seeing <ns0:hi>it is</ns0:hi> a righteous thing with God <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">It is of necessity that God should be righteous, and recompensing is a necessary act of righteousness, but we yet see it not, therefore there is a judgment to come. And this recompence is both to the righteous and the wicked, the persecutors and persecuted. The former he here speaks first of: And to recompence Tribulation to them that trouble the people of God, is a just recompence; it is according to the Law of retaliation; whereof we have some Instances in this World, as in <ns0:hi>Pharaoh, Adonibezeck, Haman, &c.</ns0:hi> and many o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers; whereof we have a large account in the History of the Church, and her Persecutors; but this will be more fully veri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fied in the Judgment to come, called, <ns0:hi>The Revelation of the Righ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teous Iudgment of God, Rom.</ns0:hi> 2.5.</ns0:note> to recompence tribulation to them that trouble you <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">And Gods recompence to them is here called tribulation, so <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 2.9. And though in other Scriptures the punishment of the wicked is set forth by other Names, yet here its called by this Name; not only for Elegancy of Speech by a <ns0:hi>Paranomasia,</ns0:hi> but to parallel their suffering to their sin, they brought tribulation upon others, and God will bring it upon them: And under this word is com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />prehended all the torments of Hell, which our Saviour expresseth by <ns0:hi>weeping, wailing,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>gnashing of Teeth, Matth.</ns0:hi> 8.12. which is the extremity of tribulation; and its said here, God will re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />compence, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> which should teach us not to revenge our selves, as <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 94.1. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 12.19. and this the Apostle sets before these <ns0:hi>Thessalonians</ns0:hi> by way of Comfort, not <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> we ought to rejoyce in mens destruction meerly for it self, but in the ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nour that will thereby arise to Gods Justice, and in the Favour, Honour, and Salvation God will vouchsafe to his people herein.</ns0:note>.<ns0:note place="bottom">By these words the Apostle doth illustrate his argument for a judgment to come, taken from the persecutions and tribula<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions of the Saints.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 And to you that are troubled, rest with us <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Having spoken of the recompence of the troublers, here of the troubled; And in this we may observe a parallel, as in the former. The recompence to these is exprest by rest; in the Greek, dismission, or cessation from labour or trouble, as <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 4.9. there remaineth a rest to the people of God, where the word is, <ns0:hi>keeping a Sabbath,</ns0:hi> importing a rest from labour, as this Text doth speak of a rest from trouble; And though the word Rest is properly Negative, yet under it the Apostle com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />prehends all the felicity of the future State; elsewhere called a Crown, a Kingdom, an Inheritance, Glory, Salvation, Eter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal Life, yea it contains in it the perfect satisfaction of the soul in the fruition of God, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> And this is said to be given them by way of recompence, as tribulation is to their troubles; though there is not parity betwixt their troubles, and the rest, that is, their recompence, yet it is a proper recompence; and therefore the Grace and Mercy of God, will be much manifest<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed therein, though its said to come from Gods Righteousness in the Text: The Righteousness of God dispenseth both these re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />compences; but yet the Righteousness in both is not alike, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> strict justice dispenseth the one, and the punish<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment of the wicked riseth from the nature of their sin, and the merit of it, but it is only <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> equity that dispenseth the other, and that not so much with respect to the nature of the Saints duties or sufferings, as the promises and ordinance of God, and the merit of Christ for them. And this rest the A<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />postle sets forth before them, under a twofold circumstance: 1. <ns0:hi>Rest with <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:hi> Us, the Apostles and Ministers of Christ, we and you shall rest together; as we have partaked of troubles together, so we shall of rest. And you shall enjoy the same felicity with the Apostles themselves, in the same state of rest. And though now place doth separate us, yet we and you shall rest together, which will the more sweeten this rest to you and us. 2.</ns0:note>, when <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Thes. 4.16.</ns0:note> the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">The other circumstance. This is the time of their entring into this rest. Christs coming is sometimes called his <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> appearing, 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 4.8. or shining <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>orth; some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />times <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> his manifestation, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 4.2. 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn.</ns0:hi> 3.2. sometimes <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> his Revelation, as in the Text. Now the Heavens co<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ain him, but he will come in person, and his Glory shine forth: Though before that their souls shall be at rest in Heaven, and their bodies in the grave<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> not till then shall their persons be at rest: And as Christ himself is already entred into his rest, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 4.10. so he will come again to take his people into the same rest with hi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> with his <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Gr. <ns0:hi>the angels of his power.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> mighty angels.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:523" />8 In flaming fire, <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 paragraph">
                        <ns0:desc>〈1 paragraph〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> taking <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 paragraph">
                        <ns0:desc>〈1 paragraph〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> vengeance <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">But his coming will be upon another account to many o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers, which is said here to be to take vengeance, for which purpose he is said to be revealed with his mighty Angels, or Angels of might; and elsewhere with all his Holy Angels. They are said to excel in strength, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 103.20. or to be mighty in strength, and have the name of mights, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 1 21. And here call'd mighty, because as the work Christ comes upon is great and difficult, so he will have instruments sufficient for it, and none shall be able to hinder. And though he hath power himself sufficient, yet the Angels must attend him to solemnize this great day, and to be serviceable to him in the work there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />of, which as it will respect the saints in their Resurrection from the dead, and their gathering from the four winds, and sepa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rating them from the ungodly, as tares from the wheat, and sheep from the goats, so the taking vengeance also in this day of the Lords wrath, which the Apostle, especially, is in these Verses speaking of, as the work they shall be employed in. <ns0:hi>As also in flaming fire,</ns0:hi> or the fire of flame, <ns0:hi>Hebraism.</ns0:hi> Fire is the most dreadful of all the Elements, especially flaming, to de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />note the great wrath of that day, and its breaking forth; as fire when it flameth. Gods wrath is often exprest in Scripture by fire, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 32.22. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 97.3. <ns0:hi>&c. Ier.</ns0:hi> 21.12. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 10.27. and as that which attendeth the great day of Christ, <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 7.10. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 3.13. 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 3.7, 12. And whether this flaming fire is Material, or only Metaphorical; if Material, whether the present Elementary fire, which shall descend, and be joined with that which shall break forth out of the Bowels of the Earth, as in <ns0:hi>Noah</ns0:hi>'s Flood, the waters were from above, and from be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />neath. Or whether it shall be some new created fire, and the action of it natural, or supernatural, I shall leave it to the school<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />men, yet its generally conceived, it is a material fire: Else how can the Elements be said to melt with fervent heat, and the World, and the works thereof burnt up, as the Apostle <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> speaks, 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 3.6. and parallels it with the deluge in <ns0:hi>Noah</ns0:hi>'s time, which was with material water, but yet it is to be a manifestation of the fire of Gods wrath, and an instrument of it also in the destruction of ungodly men, 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 3.7. for its said in the Text, Christ is revealed in it to take vengeance. Vengeance is an act of Justice: It is a retribution of evil for evil, the evil of suffering for the evil done: And God claims it as belonging to himself, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 94.1. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 1.12. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 10.27. and is mentioned in the parable, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 18.7, 8. as one great work of Christ, at his coming to avenge the Elect.</ns0:note> on them that know not God <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">These are the persons upon whom he will execute vengeance: By whom some think are meant the Heathen, who had not the Gospel. Those that had not the Gospel, yet had means to know God, by the light of Nature, and the works of Creation and Providence, which if they did not improve, but remained ig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />norant of God, will fall under this vengeance. And by know<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ledge here is not meant so much a speculative as a practical knowledge of God, and so such as do not fear, love and ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nour God, may be said not to know him. As the Gentiles who are said to know God, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 1.21. but yet not glorifying him as God, and living in Idolatry, are said not to know him, <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 4.8. 1 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 4.5. And as God tells the King of <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> that to do Justice and Judgment is to know him, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 22.16. And <ns0:hi>Eli</ns0:hi>'s Sons, though Priests, yet are said not to know the Lord, 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 2.12.</ns0:note>, and that obey not the gospel <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Which may be taken in conjunction with the former words, and then such as obey not the Gospel, are the same with them that know not God. As God is not known aright, but by the Gospel, so they only know God aright by the Gospel who obey it. Some are ignorant and know not God, though they live under the Gospel; or, such as have Know<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ledge, yet are not Obedient. Knowledge and Obedience ought to go together: And this Obedience is called the obeying of the Gospel. The Gospel hath not only promises to be believ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, but precepts to be obeyed. Yea, Faith it self may fall un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der its precepts, and then those that believe not the Gospel, do not obey it: As the same word in the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> signifies to be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieve and obey. And as the Gospel hath some peculiar precepts and institutions, so all the commands of the Moral Law are comprehend in it; and the equitable part of the Judicial Law, yea, and the Ceremonial Law also, where that which is Moral is figured By it; and so far as the Gospel commands, men ought to obey; and Disobedience appears to be a great Evil, when it will expose men to this great vengeance. So <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 2.8, 9. <ns0:hi>To them that do not obey the Truth, Indignation and Wrath, Tribulation and Anguish, &c.</ns0:hi> not to obey the Law of Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture, exposed the Heathen to Gods Wrath, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 1.18. and to disobey the Law of <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> the Jew, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 2.9. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 2.3. and 10.28. and 12.25. much more not to obey the Gospel, Christ is said here especially to take vengeance of such at his coming, Gospel sins are most hainous, and most provoking, and will be most severely punisht.</ns0:note> of our Lord Jesus Christ.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 Who shall be punished with everlasting de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />struction <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">This is the vengeance before spoken of, it is here called destruction, not an annihilation, and cessation of Being, but of all well Being: And elsewhere called Death, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 6. <ns0:hi>last.</ns0:hi> and the second Death, <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 20.6. which imports also not all ceasing of Life, but all comfort of Life. And it is not the Body alone, nor the soul alone, but their Persons; <ns0:hi>who,</ns0:hi> &c. and as fire is a great de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stroyer, so Christs coming in flaming fire, bring their destruction. And this destruction is Everlasting. The fire that destroys them is never quenched, <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 9.43, 44. As the fire of the Altar which was a fire of Mercy was not to go out, so the fire of <ns0:hi>Tophet</ns0:hi> burns for ever, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 30. <ns0:hi>last.</ns0:hi> which is the fire of Justice, and God living for ever, and his Justice never satisfied, their destruction is for ever. They sin'd in their Eternity, and will be punisht in Gods Eternity. There was a remedy provided in the Gospel for men, but rejecting the Gospel, and not obeying it, there remains no hope; their destruction is Everlasting, and this destruction is called punishment, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>poenam luent,</ns0:hi> not the chastisement of a Father as the Temporal Affli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ction of Gods people. It proceeds from vindictive Justice, it is taking vengeance. And this punishment is twofold, punish<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment of loss and sense, and from both together proceed per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fect destruction.</ns0:note>, from <ns0:note place="margin">Or, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> the presence of the Lord, and from the <ns0:note place="margin">O<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>glorious <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>,</ns0:hi> Heb.</ns0:note> glory of his power <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">The Praeposition <ns0:hi>from,</ns0:hi> in the first expressi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on noting Separation, in the second noting Efficiency. Others conceive Efficiency to be meant in both, their destruction pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceeding from the face of Christ frowning on them, frowning them into Hell, (which smiling upon others, will bring their Salvation,) as well as from his glorious Power manifested a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst them to destroy them, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 9.22. And yet others in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terpret the Praeposition in both places to note Separation, both from the face of Christ, which the Saints shall behold and re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />joice in for ever, and from his glorious Power; which will work in some for their compleat Salvation in the day of his appearing; as it had done before in their first Conversion, and Sanctification. The destruction of the wicked will be from or by the Power of Christ; but by this <ns0:hi>Glory of Power</ns0:hi> may be meant only that Power which will bring Glory both to the Bo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dies and Souls of the Saints, and this the wicked shall have no experience of in that day.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 When he shall come to be glorified in his Saints <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">This speaks the different manner of Christ coming towards the Saints and Believers, not in flaming fire to destroy them, as in the former verse; but to be glorified and admired in them. He saith not to be glorified by them, by their adoring and praising of him, but in them: He hath a personal Glory wherein he will appear glorious, and another Mystical in his Saints. The Head will be glorified in the Members, as they are glorified in and from the Head.                <ns0:p n="11">11 Wherefore <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">The Apostle here again mentions his praying for these <ns0:hi>Thessalonians,</ns0:hi> as he had o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     </ns0:gap>ten mentioned it in the former Epi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stle. And the reason might be, because he was absent from them.                         <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>wherefore</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>for,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>in order to which</ns0:hi> we pray, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> also we pray alwaies for you, that our God would <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>vouchsafe.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> count you worthy of <ns0:hi>this</ns0:hi> calling <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Which is figuratively to be understood of the blessed state they were called to, for the calling it self they had received already: And so it is the same in effect mentioned before, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 5. cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led there the Kingdom of God, or to have Christ glorified, and admired in them, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 10. And elsewhere termed the <ns0:hi>prize of the High Calling of God, Phil.</ns0:hi> 3.14. and that God would count them worthy of it; as he had used the same expression before; only there it was mentioned with respect to their sufferings here in a way of prayer. A Christians calling hath Duty annexed to it, whereupon the Apostle exhorts the <ns0:hi>Ephesians</ns0:hi> to walk worthy of it in discharge of those Duties, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 4.1, 2. But Gods account is not according to the strictness of the Law, but the gracious indulgence of the Cove<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nant of Grace, but yet his Prayer implies such a walking accor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ding to this Covenant, as whereby they might be coun<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ed wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thy of the blessed state they were called unto.</ns0:note>, and fulfil all the good pleasure of <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> goodness <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">The graci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous purposes of God towards his people are called often his good pleasure, as <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 11.26. <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 12.32. <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 1.5.9. and the same is meant <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 53.10. <ns0:hi>The pleasure of the Lord shall prosper in his hand:</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> word <ns0:hi>Chephets</ns0:hi> being of the same signification with the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> word here used. Christ shall ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />complish the gracious purposes of God towards his people, and call'dhis good pleasure, partly because they have no reason out of the Soveraign Will of God, and they are such also as he hath great complacence and delight in: And though they are exe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cuted in time, yet they were in his heart from Everlasting, and therefore call'd Eternal, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 3.11. And I find purpose and good pleasure put both together, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 1.9. and is here called the <ns0:hi>good pleasure of his goodness,</ns0:hi> which is not a tautology as it may seem to be, but to make his expression of Gods Grace the more emphatical; or rather to shew that this good <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>lea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sure of God towards his people, ariseth out of his goodness. God hath purposes of wrath towards some, but such cannot be cal'd the good pleasure of his goodness. Goodness is that excellency in God, whereby he is ready to communicate good to his Creature; but by goodness here is meantGods special good<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness which is peculiar to his people whom he hath chosen. <ns0:hi>To fulfil all the good pleasure of his goodness,</ns0:hi> is to accomplish all these good purposes that were in his heart. Some whereof were already fulfilled in their Calling, Adoption, Justification, and Sanctification begun, but the whole was not yet fulfilled, which he therefore here prays for, so that as their Election, and their first Conversion was not from any worthiness, or fore<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ight of Faith in them, but the good pleasure of his Will, so the progress and perfection of their Salvation was also to be from the same good pleasure.</ns0:note>, and the work of faith with power <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">By the work of Faith is either meant Faith it self, which is the work of God, or else the fruits of Faith; and so work is here taken for Works, or Operations of Faith. And to perfect their Salvation is a fulfilling the work of Faith, for perseverance and progress towards perfection is from the work of Faith: Or it may parti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cularly refer to their patience and constancy under their suf<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ferings which he had before spoken of, and which is a pecu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />liar work of Faith; but because Faith is not sufficient of it self, and the work of Faith may fail, he therefore addeth, <ns0:hi>in power,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>with power</ns0:hi>; that is, the power of God, which is his Spirit, so called, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 1.35. Our Faith and the Power of God are here joyned together, as 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.5. The same power that first worketh Faith, afterwards co-worketh by it, and with it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:524" />12 That the Name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and ye in him <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">

All Expositors agree that these words contain in them a final cause, as the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> word imports; and so under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand them as the ultimate end of the Apostles Prayer for them; he had prayed for things that did concern their Salvation, but he looked further, which was, that thereby the Name of the Lord Jesus may be glorified in them. The Glory of Christ, and the Saints Salvation are wrapt up together; and though they are to look immediately to the latter, yet ultimately to the former: but whether the Apostle means the glorifying Christ in this Life, or the Life to come, is a question. I rather think the words refer to the Life to come, when the Name of Christ shall be for ever glorified in the Salvation of his people, when all the good pleasure of Gods goodness shall be fulfilled upon them, they having been kept in the Faith by the power of God unto the end, through Jesus Christ; and then also they shall be glorified not only by him, as we may read the Text, but in him, in being received into a participation of the same Glory with Jesus Christ, and by their union with him, are glo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rified in him, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 17.22. <ns0:hi>Col.</ns0:hi> 3.4. 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 3.3. And hereby the Apostle would exclude all thoughts a bout their own merit, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 11.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
